newEnglishSupportReadForAlignment: **EN** Here you practise **ㅇ·ㅏ·ㅓ → 아·어**. You connect the sounds of these syllables with their written shapes; you do not need to know any meanings they may have as words. This follows your arrival at the remembered house and the request to restore it. Next come 오 and 우 in **F0.1.above-below**.

**EN** As before, ㅇ in the first position adds no consonant sound. Learn ㅗ and ㅜ as two separate letters. Notice the direction of each stroke rather than just turning a piece around. A picture of the lips or a single Roman letter cannot replace a Korean sound example.

**EN** In **F0.1.sound-signs**, you met ㅇ, ㅏ and ㅓ in 아 and 어. The new symbols here are **ㅗ·ㅜ → 오·우**. Next come ㅡ and ㅣ in **F0.1.straight-lines**. If the earlier letters are unfamiliar, you can have a short introduction before joining in.

**EN** Here you rebuild **the six syllables you have practised**. This does not test new words or your command of the whole writing system. If you have not learned a letter yet, ask to see it first. Working with that example is supported practice, and that is fine.

**EN** Do not treat the spelling eu as an English sound guide for 으. 으 is not the same sound as German ü either. Listen to the Korean example and connect it with 으. A picture alone cannot tell us how you actually pronounce it.

**EN** This follows **F0.1.above-below** and leads to **F0.2.first-names**. The new symbols are **ㅡ·ㅣ → 으·이**. You are not being asked about other meanings of 이, such as the number two or a tooth. You will learn ㄴ and ㅁ in the next unit.
